about: Articles nominated for Essential reporting, reviewed at Submissions Review > Nominated (inc/featured-nominations.php). 'note' is the draft note shown with the pick; 'reason' is for the reviewer only. Tier 2 = good, ranked lower. Bump version to add new ones; a nomination already decided is never changed.

nominations.note: The Bee's 1998 series on California sending its young people to out-of-state camps with little oversight, begun after Nicholaus Contreraz died at Arizona Boys Ranch.
nominations.reason: Original multi-part investigation (1998, Sam Stanton and Mareva Brown) with documented results; the follow-ups (1011-1025) are stored too.

nominations.note: Mystie Kreimeyer was 15 when she died at Forest Ridge, a for-profit home in Iowa, after staff were slow to get her emergency care. Iowa later cited the home for its emergency care and its restraints.
nominations.reason: Nina Bernstein, New York Times, 1997: early national reporting on for-profit placements.

nominations.note: Gina Score, 14, collapsed on a run at a South Dakota state boot camp and died of heatstroke while staff took her collapse for defiance. Bruce Selcraig's account of the camp and the system around it.
nominations.reason: Mother Jones, 2000: long-form investigation.

nominations.note: Pamela Colloff's history of Lester Roloff's Rebekah Home for Girls: the punishments survivors describe, and the decades of fights over whether Texas could license it.
nominations.reason: Texas Monthly, 2001: long-form history built on survivor accounts and court records.

nominations.note: How the Judge Rotenberg Center used electric shock and other aversives on disabled students, the deaths and injuries there, and how lawmakers and regulators responded.
nominations.reason: Paul Kix, Boston Magazine, 2008.

nominations.note: New York City was paying the Judge Rotenberg Center $30 million a year. ProPublica followed the money and the center's record of violations.
nominations.reason: Heather Vogell and Annie Waldman, ProPublica, 2014: follows public money.

nominations.note: Chris Kirkham's investigation of Youth Services International and its owner, James Slattery: abuse, medical neglect and unreported incidents across the company's juvenile facilities, alongside its lobbying for privatization.
nominations.reason: HuffPost, 2013: company-wide investigation.

nominations.note: The Inquirer documented years of sexual abuse by staff at Devereux facilities in several states, and how the warning signs were dismissed.
nominations.reason: Lisa Gartner and Barbara Laker, Philadelphia Inquirer, 2020.

nominations.note: APM Reports and OPB traced a pattern of violence, sexual assault and improper restraint across Sequel's facilities for foster children in more than 40 states.
nominations.reason: Curtis Gilbert and Lauren Dake, 2020: the investigation behind much of the later Sequel coverage.

nominations.note: The Associated Press found adopted children sent to for-profit treatment programs, where many were restrained, abused or neglected.
nominations.reason: AP series, 2026 (also #111 and #184). The author field is empty, so it shows without a byline.

nominations.note: The Missoulian found 58 complaints in 12 years against Montana's private youth programs and no sanctions from a board made up mostly of industry representatives.
nominations.reason: Missoulian series, 2019; #678 is the companion piece on owners and administrators.

nominations.note: The Missoulian mapped the owners and administrators who moved between Montana programs, several of them with past license revocations or criminal charges.
nominations.reason: Missoulian series, 2019.

nominations.note: Will Craft showed how Utah's licensers let a Provo Canyon School restraint that left a disabled teen with an untreated concussion go uncited, and that it was not the only one.
nominations.reason: Salt Lake Tribune, 2021: records-based.

nominations.note: Of 1,154 calls to Colorado's child abuse hotline from youth treatment centers in five years, 92% were screened out. Jennifer Brown's investigation for The Colorado Sun.
nominations.reason: Colorado Sun, 2026: data investigation.

nominations.note: ProPublica and WPLN found that Wayne Halfway House did not report suspected abuse at its Tennessee juvenile facilities. The state opened an investigation after the reporting.
nominations.reason: Paige Pfleger and Aliyya Swaby, 2026; #292 and #390 are follow-ups.

nominations.note: Sara Gentzler's reporting on the investigation into Nebraska's youth center at Kearney: 44 sexual abuse allegations from 37 boys against 19 staff, and the culture that let it go on.
nominations.reason: Flatwater Free Press, 2026; part of a long run of Kearney coverage.

nominations.note: At least 90 former students of the Family Foundation School in New York have died since it closed in 2014, most of overdoses and suicide. Michael Wilson asked why.
nominations.reason: New York Times, 2018.

nominations.note: At least 34 boys from the Dozier School and 16 from Okeechobee ended up on Florida's death row. Leonora LaPeter Anton's investigation for The Marshall Project and the Tampa Bay Times.
nominations.reason: 2025. The Tampa Bay Times' earlier Dozier reporting is not stored yet (it waits in the SCIAD NET links at Drive Docs).

nominations.note: Ashlynd Baecht's investigation of New Lifehouse Academy, an unlicensed Christian program for girls in rural Oklahoma: restraint, food restriction and unpaid labor, by former students' accounts.
nominations.reason: The Frontier, 2026. This copy has no date; #369 and #531 are the dated follow-ups.

nominations.note: Court records, police reports and former students' accounts of Spring Ridge Academy in Arizona.
nominations.reason: Sebastian Murdock and Taiyler Mitchell, HuffPost, 2025. You said it won an award: name the award in the note.

nominations.note: The New Yorker on the programs struggling children are sent to, Teen Challenge among them, and the transport agents who take them there.
nominations.reason: 2021. The author field is empty, so it shows without a byline until the article is edited.

nominations.note: Rachel Browne's account of Robert Land Academy in Ontario, where two boys died trying to escape in 1998 and staff used their deaths to frighten students for years.
nominations.reason: The Walrus, 2024: long-form.

nominations.note: Riley Board's reporting on former students' accounts of forced labor and humiliating punishment at Hyde School in Bath, Maine.
nominations.reason: Central Maine, 2025: the reporting that opened up Hyde. #25 'Revisiting Hyde' is the follow-up.

nominations.note: WPLN on Kingston Academy, a Sequel psychiatric center in Tennessee where inexperienced, overworked staff left children without care. It closed after the state investigated.
nominations.reason: Natasha Senjanovic, 2020.

nominations.note: Tony Cook found that an Indiana child services worker told Pierceton Woods Academy the date and time of a surprise inspection.
nominations.reason: Indianapolis Star, 2025: records-based.

nominations.note: Staff at the Wyoming Boys' School testified that they were told to falsify records to play down the force they used.
nominations.reason: Maya Shimizu Harris, WyoFile, 2026.

nominations.note: Jennifer Kovaleski's reporting on Mingus Mountain Academy for ABC15 led a state senator to call for an investigation.
nominations.reason: 2025. ABC15's original investigation is not stored; if you add it, it is the better pick.

nominations.note: NBC News on the money Sequel's youth facilities made while children in its care were reportedly abused.
nominations.reason: 2020; a strong second on Sequel after #946.

nominations.note: Inside Calo Programs in Missouri, a taxpayer-funded treatment center for adoptees: an Associated Press look at abuse, neglect and little oversight.
nominations.reason: Part of the AP adoptees series (#172).

nominations.note: ProPublica on Mount Pleasant Academy in Utah, raided after staff reported misconduct and sexual abuse between residents.
nominations.reason: Joaquin Sapien, 2016.

nominations.note: The Berkshire Edge on the state report that found a systemic cover-up of abuse by the Eagleton School's administration.
nominations.reason: Heather Bellow, 2016; she covered Eagleton through its closure and the criminal cases.

nominations.note: A 15-year-old from San Francisco died after an incident at Rite of Passage's desert boot camp in Nevada.
nominations.reason: San Francisco Chronicle, 1992: early coverage.

nominations.note: Police records and child safety reports showing staff assaulting students at Canyon State Academy in Arizona.
nominations.reason: Justin Lum, FOX 10, 2023: records-based.

nominations.note: Former Hyde School students on how the abuse allegations reopened what they went through.
nominations.reason: Riley Board, Central Maine, 2025: follow-up to #34.
